name: English
title: Open Agent Systems — AI development tools and infrastructure
description: Open Agent Systems is an open-source organization working on AI development tools, agent infrastructure, and interoperability.
label: An open-source organization
headline:
Toward AI-native.
Built to connect.
intro: Open Agent Systems (OAS) explores what comes after a single model call: intelligent systems that collaborate, compose, and keep running.
introMore: Through open source, we aim to turn emerging capabilities into foundations developers can use, connect, and operate.
aboutText: AI development reaches beyond the model. Tools need to work together, execution needs to be manageable, and developers need to understand what their systems are doing. These are the problems we want to work on.
areas: Bring AI into coding, testing, delivery, and collaboration, with attention to the everyday developer experience.
Make skills, tools, and workflows reusable, so applications can be assembled around real needs.
Improve execution environments, deployment, resource management, and observability for AI workloads.
Help independent tools and projects work together without repeated, one-off integration work.
directionIntro: We expect the work to move from individual tools toward connected systems. Each step should build on working software and lessons from its users.
diagramTitle: Long-term direction: useful tools, manageable systems, interoperable capabilities, and a shared ecosystem
steps: Turn emerging capabilities into usable tools. Validate their value in real development scenarios, with documentation, examples, and a considered user experience.
Move from one-off experiments toward sustained operation. Make deployment, scheduling, state, and observability understandable and manageable.
Compose models, agents, and tools through clear interfaces. Reduce repeated integration work while preserving the freedom to replace components.
Help independent projects share foundations. Evolve the ecosystem through open collaboration, documentation, and feedback from practice.
feedbackLoop: Real use and community feedback inform every stage.
directionNote: This diagram describes our intended direction, not a release schedule or a statement of completed capabilities. Work in these areas may overlap; priorities will follow actual needs and available contributions.
principles: Prefer small, composable capabilities with understandable interfaces.
Documentation, examples, and maintainability matter alongside implementation.
Be clear about what is available, what has been verified, and what is still being explored.
joinText: Have a use case, an integration problem, or an idea for the ecosystem? Tell us what you’re trying to do, what is getting in the way, and what you’ve already tried.
joinNote: Organization-level suggestions are welcome in the community repository’s Issues. Contributions to individual projects will be handled in their own repositories when they are published.
footer: Open-source tools and infrastructure for AI development.
architectureIntro: A target capability map for the organization—not the deployment architecture of a single product. Independent projects can contribute at different layers.
architectureNote: Planning view · These capabilities are areas to develop, not a claim of completed delivery.
architectureHint: Select a layer to explore its role.
layers: The user-facing layer: tools and applications that solve specific development and collaboration problems.
Reusable capabilities with clear interfaces. Projects should be able to compose what they need without adopting the entire ecosystem.
The execution layer: environments and operational tools that make AI workloads easier to deploy, inspect, and manage.
visionTitle: Make AI capabilities an open, shared foundation.
visionText: We want developers to choose their models, compose agents and tools, and run systems in environments they can control. Independent projects should share foundations, and contributors should help them evolve—making advances in AI useful to more people.
exploreNote: Concept exploration · Select a node to see its role
exploreItems: Connect different models so applications can choose and switch capabilities for the task.
Combine models, skills, and tools into execution units that can carry out tasks.
Bring external tools and data into intelligent systems through understandable interfaces.
Provide observable, manageable environments for intelligent execution.
Compose underlying capabilities into products developers and teams can actually use.
